# Actual generated Bytes body field composition

`NativeBodyLength` derives actual Core body length/presence/counter/mode from
actual native length success on every input, without a caller prefix/table
premise. If declared length exceeds physical remaining input, actual Core
rejects at actual EOF: no padding byte is supplied or borrowed.

`BodyDispatch` composes the actual generated response body field with the actual
Bytes replacement merger and native length decoder. It retains exact source
content/suffix, absent default initialization, duplicate replacement, errors and
diagnostic-stack effects, including fail/div. `BodyFieldRefinement` joins all
input/outcome cases: native varint errors and physical Bytes underflow reject
Core; successful source copy is exact and its content length equals the native
decoded count, while Core length/presence/counter/mode correspond. Empty bodies
and arbitrary body bytes are included.

The theorem does not yet relate the complete emitted body-byte trace or prove
Core valid stays255 for a successful source message. Child-limit overruns with
physically available outer bytes, successful payload-state preservation, other
fields/groups/private EOF, HTTP/correlation/compiler composition remain open.
Source failed-record/error effects remain explicit before owned observation.
Inherited Bytes allocation/reference-count/content, diagnostic static-push and
other std model boundaries remain unchanged.

Run `check_body_field.py` for an isolated immutable three-module kernel check
with verified ancestor sources/objects.
